items.title: Ukraine says Russia recruited 27,000 from 135 countries

featured_image.name: Russia increases recruitment of foreign fighters through ...

items.description: Ukraine's military intelligence has identified 27,407 nationals from 135 countries recruited into Russia's armed forces, according to data released on March 30. The figures underscore what the European Parliament has classified as human trafficking, as Moscow turns to deceptive recruitment across Africa, Cuba, and Central Asia to replenish its frontline forces more than four years into its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.[1][2]

items.title: Rubio chastises NATO allies for inaction during Iran war

featured_image.name: Rubio tells Al Jazeera that Strait of Hormuz to reopen 'one way or ...

items.description:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio used an exclusive Al Jazeera interview published Monday to chastise NATO allies for their inaction during the U.S.-led war in Iran, questioning "what is in it for the United States" if the alliance fails to support American military objectives. The remarks echo language Rubio first used in January before a Senate committee, when he declared that "without the U.S., there is no NATO", a line that has become a recurring theme as the conflict tests transatlantic solidarity.[1][2][3]

The wide-ranging interview, segments of which Al Jazeera released throughout the day, saw Rubio outline U.S. demands for Iran and assert that the Strait of Hormuz would "reopen one way or another" once the war concludes. He warned Tehran of "serious repercussions" if it continued blocking the waterway and said President Trump "always prefers diplomacy," noting that indirect talks between the two sides are underway through intermediaries.[4][5][6][7]

items.title: Trump floats asking Arab states to help pay for Iran war

featured_image.name: Trump Seems to Embrace 'Regime Change' in Iran - TIME

items.description:
President Donald Trump is interested in calling on Arab countries to help cover the costs of the war in Iran, White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt indicated during a briefing on Monday, as the month-old conflict's price tag continues to climb and diplomatic efforts intensify across the region.[1][2][3]

The remarks come as the Pentagon has already estimated the war's first six days alone cost more than $11.3 billion, with independent analysts projecting total spending may have exceeded $25 billion by late March. Trump has previously called on Middle Eastern allies — including Saudi Arabia, Qatar, the UAE, Bahrain, and Kuwait — to take on greater responsibility in the conflict, including policing the Strait of Hormuz.[4][5][6][7]

items.title: Israel Knesset passes death penalty law for Palestinians

featured_image.name: Israel Knesset set to vote on death penalty law for ...

items.description:
Israel's parliament voted on Monday to impose the death penalty on Palestinians in the West Bank convicted of deadly attacks against Israelis, a move that drew immediate international condemnation and is expected to face a swift legal challenge before the country's Supreme Court.

The Knesset passed the measure 62–48 after nearly twelve hours of debate, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu personally voting in favor in the final moments. The law represents a major victory for far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, whose Otzma Yehudit party has long championed the legislation.[1]

items.title: NATO intercepts fourth Iranian missile over Turkey

featured_image.name: NATO defences destroy missile fired from Iran over Mediterranean

items.description:
NATO air and missile defense systems deployed in the Eastern Mediterranean intercepted a fourth Iranian ballistic missile entering Turkish airspace on Monday, Turkey's Defense Ministry reported, extending a pattern of alarming incursions that has tested the alliance's readiness and complicated Ankara's dual role as both a NATO member and diplomatic intermediary in the wider conflict.[1]

The ministry stated that "all necessary measures are being taken decisively and without hesitation against any threat directed at our country's territory and airspace," language consistent with its prior statements on similar incidents. It did not disclose the missile's type, trajectory, or intended target.[2]

items.title: 3 Indonesian UNIFIL peacekeepers killed in Lebanon in 24 hours

featured_image.name: One UNIFIL peacekeeper killed, another wounded in southern ...

items.description: Three Indonesian peacekeepers serving with the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon were killed in two separate incidents in southern Lebanon within 24 hours on March 29-30, marking the deadliest stretch for the mission since the Israel-Hezbollah conflict reignited on March 2.

items.title: Trump confirms US is negotiating with Iran's Ghalibaf

featured_image.name: Iran's Parliament speaker takes center role in peace talks

items.description:
President Donald Trump on Monday publicly identified Iranian Parliamentary Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf as the person the United States has been negotiating with to end the war with Iran, telling the New York Post that "we'll find out in about a week" whether Ghalibaf is someone America can work with.[1]

The confirmation ends days of speculation after Trump last week announced on Truth Social that "very good and productive conversations" were taking place between Washington and Tehran without naming his counterpart. Trump had previously described the official only as "a top person" who is "highly respected".[2][3]

items.title: Renoir, Cezanne, Matisse paintings stolen in 3-minute Italian museum heist

featured_image.name: Paintings 'worth millions' stolen from museum in Italy | World News

items.description: Four masked thieves broke into one of Italy's most prestigious private museums on the night of March 22–23 and made off with three masterpieces worth an estimated €9 million (£7.8 million) in a raid that lasted less than three minutes, authorities confirmed on Sunday.[1][2]

items.title: Trump weighs sending troops into Iran to seize uranium

featured_image.name: Trump faces his most difficult Iran war decision: Will he deploy ... - PBS

items.description: President Donald Trump is considering a military operation to extract nearly 1,000 pounds of enriched uranium from Iranian nuclear sites, The Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, a move that would mark a dramatic escalation in a war now entering its fifth week. No final decision has been made, but officials say Trump remains open to the idea, which aligns with his stated goal of ensuring Iran never develops a nuclear weapon.[1][2]

items.title: Sungrazing comet, meteor shower and Artemis II set up a historic April sky

featured_image.name: New 'sungrazing' comet could become visible to the naked eye ...

items.description: New Yorkers who look up this April could witness a month of celestial events unlike any in recent memory. A newly discovered sungrazing comet is racing toward its dramatic encounter with the Sun, the annual Lyrid meteor shower will streak across dark skies, and NASA is preparing to send astronauts toward the Moon for the first time in more than half a century.

items.title: Iran calls US 15-point peace proposal 'unrealistic' as Trump threatens Kharg Island seizure

featured_image.name: Esmail Baghaei: Iran, US Held Intensive Three-Hour Talks in ...

items.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei rejected reports of direct negotiations with Washington, declaring that a 15-point US peace proposal conveyed through intermediaries was "excessive and unrealistic," as the month-old conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran showed fresh signs of widening across the region.

items.title: Trump threatens to destroy Iran's energy sites if no deal reached

featured_image.name: Trump threatens Iran with bombs unless nuclear deal reached

items.description: President Donald Trump on Monday escalated his rhetoric against Iran, threatening to destroy the country's electric generating plants, oil wells, and Kharg Island if a peace deal is not reached "shortly" and the Strait of Hormuz is not immediately reopened to shipping. The threats came even as Trump claimed diplomatic progress was being made — a characterization Tehran flatly denies.

items.title: Guardian profiles UN chief tasked with planetary defense

featured_image.name: Message from Aarti Holla-Maini, Director of the United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs

items.description: Aarti Holla-Maini, director of the United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs, sits at the center of a global early-warning chain designed to alert every nation on Earth when an asteroid threatens the planet. A profile published by The Guardian on Sunday described her as "primed and ready should a planetary strike occur" — a readiness that was put to the test just over a year ago when asteroid 2024 YR4 triggered the first formal warning to all UN member states under existing planetary defense protocols.[1][2]

items.title: TotalEnergies reaps over $1B from historic Middle East oil bet

featured_image.name: TotalEnergies corners Middle East crude market, reaping record profits

items.description: TotalEnergies made more than $1 billion in profit this month by cornering the Middle Eastern crude oil market during one of the most volatile periods in energy trading history, according to reporting by the Financial Times and Bloomberg.[1][2]

items.title: Middle East war drives inflation higher in New Zealand, Germany

featured_image.name: Treasury predicting 3.7% inflation in Iran war 'worst case ...

items.description:
The escalating war in the Middle East is pushing inflation above central bank targets in New Zealand and Germany, as surging energy prices ripple through both economies and complicate the outlook for monetary policy.

In New Zealand, Finance Minister Nicola Willis warned on Monday that inflation is likely to climb well above the Reserve Bank's 1–3% target band this year if the conflict persists. Treasury modeling projects inflation could reach 3.7% under a worst-case scenario in which the war drags on and oil prices rise to US$135 a barrel, Willis told reporters. Annual inflation already stood at 3.1% in the December 2025 quarter, above both the central bank's target range and its own forecasts.[1][2][3][4]

In Germany, state-level data released Monday pointed to a sharp acceleration in consumer prices. Inflation in North Rhine-Westphalia, the country's most populous state, jumped to 2.7% in March from 1.8% in February, with similar increases across Baden-Württemberg and Lower Saxony. Bloomberg Economics estimated that national inflation likely rose to 2.8% in March, up from 1.9% in February — the highest reading in over a year. Germany's Federal Statistical Office, Destatis, is set to release the official national figure later on Monday.[5][6]

items.title: Researchers build laser that controls sound particles for jam-proof navigation

featured_image.name: US team makes phonon lasers as a step towards 'unjammable' navigation

items.description: Researchers at the University of Rochester and Rochester Institute of Technology have created a new type of laser that controls particles of sound rather than light, a development they say could one day help build navigation systems immune to jamming. The work, published March 30 in Nature Communications, describes the first two-mode thermomechanically squeezed phonon laser — a device that produces coherent, low-noise vibrations using an optically levitated nanoparticle.[1][2]

items.title: Gold holds near $4,490 as surging oil kills Fed rate cut hopes

featured_image.name: Gold futures in New York whipsaw as tariff confusion sweeps precious metal  market

items.description: Gold prices held steady near $4,490 per ounce as the final week of March drew to a close, with the precious metal caught between safe-haven demand from the escalating Middle East conflict and downward pressure from surging oil prices that have all but extinguished hopes for Federal Reserve rate cuts this year.[1][2]

items.title: US stock futures slide as Iran war enters fifth week

featured_image.name: The S&P 500 could join other U.S. benchmarks in a correction next week. Here's what's ahead

items.description:
US stock futures dropped on Sunday night as investors grappled with the economic fallout of the Iran war and braced for a critical jobs report at the end of a holiday-shortened trading week.

Dow Jones Industrial Average futures slid more than 300 points, or 0.7%, late Sunday, while S&P 500 futures fell 0.7% and Nasdaq-100 futures dropped 0.8%, according to MarketWatch. The declines followed a bruising Friday session that pushed the Dow into correction territory — a drop of at least 10% from a recent high — joining the Nasdaq, which had already crossed that threshold. The S&P 500 closed at its lowest level since last July.[1]

items.title: Trump claims progress on Iran peace plan as Tehran denies any talks

featured_image.name: Iran has received Trump's 15-point plan to end war, report says

items.description: President Donald Trump claimed Sunday that Iran has agreed to "most" of the demands in a 15-point peace proposal the United States delivered through Pakistani intermediaries, describing talks aimed at ending the month-old war as going "very well." But the assertion was swiftly contradicted by Iranian officials, who denied any negotiations are underway and accused Washington of pursuing surrender terms disguised as diplomacy.

items.title: Pakistan offers to host U.S.-Iran talks after Hormuz summit

featured_image.name: Will host US-Iran talks in coming days: Pakistan after meeting with ...

items.description: Foreign ministers from Turkey, Egypt, and Saudi Arabia gathered in Islamabad on Sunday for talks aimed at ending the month-old war between the United States and Iran, with discussions centered on proposals to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to global shipping.
